methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Neuromeka is a public robotics and manufacturing company listed on KOSDAQ that has raised $36.5M in total capital. The valuation universe includes one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private-sector peers spanning robotics and automation, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable in this case. Despite identifying eight same-sector peers, none satisfy the filtering criteria for reliable comparable analysis—specifically, no peers exist at the same development stage, adjacent stage, or within a similar valuation tier. This scarcity prevents construction of a sufficiently robust peer set (minimum three datapoints required) that would justify a median-based valuation without material distortion risk. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity across company maturity, technology focus, and market position.

Without viable triangulation methods supported by sufficient comparable data, this analysis cannot produce a defensible valuation range at this time. The primary constraint is structural: Neuromeka's public status and accumulated capital raise of $36.5M position it in a narrow tier within robotics where comparable companies either cluster substantially higher or lower in development stage. Resolution would require either expansion of the comparable universe through private transaction data or application of fundamental methods (DCF, sum-of-parts) if forward financial projections become available.
